title: The erased title
hookLine: the Meccan envoy objects to "Messenger of Allah" in the treaty; Ali won't erase it, so the Prophet ﷺ erases it himself (Bukhari; Muslim)

cards: A treaty is being written at Hudaybiyyah. Ali ibn Abi Talib holds the pen. Across from the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ sits Suhayl ibn Amr, sent by Mecca to make terms.
Everyone around them is tense: they came as pilgrims, they've been turned back, a friend was feared dead. Now they're arguing about what to put on paper.
And, as Sahih al-Bukhari tells it, Suhayl objects to the very first line. Today: the erased title.

teach.b: The Prophet tells Ali to write: in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Suhayl says: the Beneficent, al-Rahman? I don't know what that is.
Write: in Your name, O Allah, as you used to write. The Muslims want the full line. The Prophet says: write it his way.

Next: this is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to. Suhayl stops him again. If we believed you were the Messenger of Allah, he says, we wouldn't have kept you from the House or fought you.

teach.h: I AM THE MESSENGER OF ALLAH, EVEN IF YOU DENY ME.
teach.b: And the Prophet answers: by Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me. Write Muhammad, son of Abdullah.
In al-Bara's report, in Bukhari, the Prophet tells Ali to erase the words, Messenger of Allah, and Ali says: no, by Allah, I will never erase it.
Some readers hear love in that, not stubbornness: he can't bring himself to rub out the title of the man he follows.
Sahih Muslim adds the detail: the Prophet says, show me where it is. Ali shows him the place on the page, and the Prophet erases it with his own hand. Notice what he gave up, and what he didn't.
He never stopped saying who he was; he said it out loud, to Suhayl's face.
What he let go of was the word on the page. At the kneeling camel he had already said it: any plan that honors what Allah made sacred, he would grant. And notice Ali.
The reports record no rebuke for his refusal. The Prophet simply did it himself.

how: The treaty of Hudaybiyyah is taught in sirah classes and in commentaries on Surah al-Fath, and the erased title is retold as an example of the Prophet's patience in making peace.

he said: by Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me. only the page changed.

games.q: you're writing a peace treaty, and the other side refuses to let your title stand. your closest companion won't erase it. what do you do?
o: insist on the title; the treaty can wait.
ask to be shown the place, and erase it yourself.
order your companion to erase it.
games.why: he said, show me where it is, and erased it with his own hand, while saying aloud: I am the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me.

practice: Think of an argument you're in, at home, at work, in a group chat, that's stuck on a word: an apology worded just so, a title, whose name goes on top. Ask the Prophet's question: am I giving up what's true, or only the wording?
If the truth stays true either way, picture yourself taking the pen and erasing the word yourself; if you pray, you can ask Allah for peace between you.

wordCard.voice: Suhayl, the Meccan negotiator who objected to the treaty's first lines until the Prophet erased his own title rather than lose the peace. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Messenger of Allah, the title erased from the page at Hudaybiyyah.

carryVoice: Your line: peace over pride. He kept the truth and let the word go. Day seven hundred eighty-six.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732 (Suhayl objects to 'al-Rahman' and to 'Messenger of Allah'; 'I am the Messenger of Allah even if you deny me')
Sahih al-Bukhari 2699 (al-Bara: Ali refuses to erase the title)
Sahih Muslim 1783 ('show me its place', and he erased it)
